business_problem: Snappt is an applicant trust platform for the rental housing industry, helping property management companies verify identity, income and rental payment history so they can reduce fraud and bad debt. Snappt’s property management customers have been asking for richer analytics for years: fraud trends, aggregated insights and hard proof of Snappt’s ROI across their portfolios.
solution_summary: Snappt built its Databricks implementation around AI/BI, Databricks Data + AI Platform, Databricks SQL, Unity Catalog. Snappt is an applicant trust platform for the rental housing industry, helping property management companies verify identity, income and rental payment history so they can reduce fraud and bad debt. Snappt’s property management customers have been asking for richer analytics for years: fraud trends, aggregated insights and hard proof of Snappt’s ROI across their portfolios. AI/BI delivers business intelligence and semantic analytics over curated Databricks data. Databricks Data + AI Platform provides the shared lakehouse environment for ingestion, engineering, analytics, and AI workflows in this deployment. Databricks SQL serves governed analytics, dashboards, and ad hoc queries for business users and operational teams. Unity Catalog applies centralized governance, lineage, auditing, and access control across shared data assets.

data_flow: Source data is ingested into databricks, curated in shared lakehouse tables, processed with Databricks compute and orchestration services, and served through analytics, semantic search, or model endpoints for downstream users and applications.
business_outcome: For customers, the dashboards turn verified data into clear, visual insights that are easy to explore without waiting on a CSM. Property admins can compare fraud rates by building and region, understand aggregated applicant demographics and quantify the financial impact of Snappt in terms that matter to owners.

Snappt serves property management companies that oversee large multifamily portfolios, from 100-unit buildings to thousands of units.
Over time, they plan to extend access to their broader base of 22,000 leasing agents.
evidence_quotes: Early attempts to meet this demand relied on internal Tableau dashboards and manual reporting. Customer success managers would screenshot charts, assemble QBR decks and manually slice data for each customer request.
“Every quarter, embedded dashboards have come up in our roadmap conversations,” Briana Ings, Chief Product and Technology Officer at Snappt, said. “It always looked like a big rock.
“I spun up a dashboard in Databricks and coded a simple standalone app one night after my kids went to bed,” she said. “It took about four hours to get from idea to a working prototype.”
